result.text: For coursework submitted up to 5 working days after the deadline without approved mitigating circumstances, a penalty of 3% of the total available mark is deducted per working day. Any coursework submitted more than 5 working days late will automatically receive a mark of zero. If you have valid reasons for a late submission, you should submit a Mitigating Circumstances application as soon as possible. Please consult your course handbook or course coordinator for specific guidelines regarding your module.

If you submit your coursework late, there is a 30% mark deduction penalty for up to 5 working days [1]. Submitting after 5 working days results in a mark of 0F (fail) and no feedback [1]. However, if valid mitigating circumstances are approved, penalties may be waived or removed [2][3].

Under Heriot-Watt University policy, coursework submitted more than 5 working days after the published deadline will not be marked and will automatically receive a mark of zero. Therefore, if you hand in your coursework 7 working days late, it will not be marked. If you experienced severe, unexpected circumstances that prevented you from submitting on time, you should submit a Mitigating Circumstances application as soon as possible.

If you submit coursework after 5 working days late, you will receive a mark of 0F (fail) and no feedback [1]. Therefore, if you submit coursework 7 working days late, it will not receive feedback and will be awarded a 0F grade unless mitigating circumstances are approved [1]. If mitigating circumstances are approved, late submission penalties may be waived or removed [1][2][5].

Lecturers at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia cannot grant informal assignment extensions directly. To request an extension, you must submit a formal Mitigating Circumstances (MC) application through the Student Portal before your assignment deadline. You will need to provide supporting evidence, such as a medical certificate or relevant documentation, with your application. For assistance with the process, you can contact your Academic Support Advisor or the Student Wellbeing team.

Under university policy, no individual extensions are allowed for coursework [2]. Class-wide extensions are permitted only in exceptional circumstances [1]. However, individual accommodations may apply where formally agreed as reasonable adjustments, or late submission penalties may be waived if valid mitigating circumstances are approved [1][2].

No, the standard late submission penalties do not apply to class tests or presentations. Missing a scheduled test or presentation without prior authorization will generally result in a mark of zero. If you are unable to attend due to valid, unforeseen circumstances, you must submit a Mitigating Circumstances application to be considered for an alternative assessment opportunity.
No, late penalties do not apply to them, as presentations, online tests, and other time-limited activities are classified as excluded assessments [2].

Yes, a Course Leader can extend a coursework deadline for the whole class if there are valid, cohort-wide reasons such as technical disruptions or schedule adjustments. Any blanket extension will be formally communicated to all enrolled students via Canvas or official university email. Please note that individual extension requests due to personal reasons must be submitted through the university's Mitigating Circumstances process instead.
Class-wide extensions for coursework are allowed only in exceptional circumstances [2]. Otherwise, individual extensions are not permitted [1].

You must submit any missing supporting documents within **10 working days** of submitting your Mitigating Circumstances application. If you cannot obtain the required evidence within this timeframe due to delays beyond your control, you should notify the Student Hub or your School Office immediately. All supporting evidence must be received before the Mitigating Circumstances Committee meets to review your application.

You have ten working days to provide any requested missing documentation for a mitigating circumstances application [1][2]. If you do not provide the documentation within this timeframe, your application will expire and be marked as Closed [1][2].

At Heriot-Watt University, you can self-certify for mitigating circumstances for up to 5 consecutive calendar days without providing official evidence. If your circumstances affect you for longer than 5 days, you must submit independent supporting evidence, such as a medical certificate or doctor's note. Please ensure you submit your application via the Student Portal within the required timeframe.
You can self-certify mitigating circumstances for a period of no more than seven days [1].

A successful mitigating circumstances application at Heriot-Watt University will not result in your marks or grades being directly increased. Instead, it can lead to outcomes such as an extension on coursework submission deadlines, an uncapped deferred assessment (treated as a first attempt), or having an affected attempt set aside. Additionally, the Exam Board may take your circumstances into account when making decisions regarding your academic progression or final degree classification.

A successful mitigating circumstances application can result in various academic mitigations recommended by the Mitigating Circumstances Board [3]. Possible outcomes include removing a 30% late penalty on coursework, offering a resit as the same opportunity, or allowing dissertation submission at the next opportunity [3]. The board may also disregard an affected assessment component to recalculate the grade, map a mark to the next higher grade threshold, or present the case to a progression or award board [3][5]. In exceptional circumstances, a combination of these approved mitigations may also be applied [5].

No, a mitigating circumstances claim will generally not be accepted without suitable supporting evidence. Heriot-Watt University requires independent, official documentation—such as a medical certificate or police report—to substantiate your claim. Submitting a claim without evidence will usually result in it being rejected. If you are having difficulty obtaining evidence, please reach out to your Personal Tutor or the Student Wellbeing team for advice.

A mitigating circumstances application will be marked as Not Accepted (Reject) if the student does not provide any or sufficient evidence to support it [1][3]. However, a student may submit a self-certification form if the mitigating circumstances period is for no more than seven days and a reason is provided for why evidence could not be given [1]. For undergraduate programmes, the minimum mark required to pass a course is a Grade D (40%), whereas for postgraduate programmes, it is a Grade C (50%). Core courses generally must be passed outright and cannot be passed via compensation. Please check your specific Programme Handbook or consult your Academic Support Advisor for detailed requirements for your degree.
A Grade D is the minimum requirement to pass core courses [1].

For undergraduate programmes at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia, the lowest grade that awards credit points is a **Grade D** (40%). For postgraduate programmes, the minimum passing grade required to earn credit points is typically a **Grade C** (50%). Any grades below these thresholds are considered fails and will not yield any credit points.
Grade E is the minimum requirement for gaining credit points for a course [1]. In contrast, Grade F does not carry any credits [2].

Under standard Heriot-Watt University regulations, you are normally permitted **one** resit (re-assessment) opportunity per failed course. If you do not pass the resit, you may be required to repeat the course in full in a subsequent semester, subject to your programme's progression rules. Please note that certain professional accreditation bodies or specific programmes may have stricter limits. For detailed guidance on your specific course, please contact your Personal Tutor or the Academic Registry.

One re-assessment opportunity is permitted for each course [2]. Re-assessments should usually be taken at the next available diet, which is typically in August [2]. If you need to defer a re-assessment until the next academic session, you must first seek permission from your School [2].

No, you do not receive any credits for an F grade at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia. An F grade represents a fail, which means you have not met the required learning outcomes for the course. To earn the credits, you will need to successfully pass the course through reassessment or by retaking it. Please contact your Academic Advisor or Director of Studies for guidance on your next steps.
No, a Grade F does not carry any credits [1].

Please check the Heriot-Watt University Malaysia website or contact the Admissions Office directly for the latest updates on future fees.
For international Computing Science students in 2026/27, the tuition fee per semester is RM 24,200.00 [1]. Including 6% SST, the total fee per semester is RM 25,652.00 [1].

No, tuition fees for educational services at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia are exempt from Malaysian Service Tax (SST) for both local and international students. However, certain non-tuition administrative or ancillary charges may still be subject to prevailing government taxes. For a detailed breakdown of your specific invoice, please contact the HWUM Finance department.

Yes, a 6% service tax (SST) will be charged to non-Malaysian students in accordance with expanded SST regulations effective 1 July 2025 [1][5]. The University also reserves the right to revise the total payable amount if there are future changes to the SST rate or the introduction of other taxes [1][5].

I do not know the exact current registration fee as it varies depending on your programme level and required visa processing (EMGS) charges. Please check the official Heriot-Watt University Malaysia website
The non-refundable registration fee for international students is RM500 plus 6% SST, which totals RM530 [2].

Tuition fees are generally due by the payment deadline specified on your fee invoice, which is typically prior to the start of the semester or within the first week of classes. If you are paying via an approved installment plan, your payments must follow the dates outlined in your agreed payment schedule. You can view your specific invoice and due dates on the Student Portal or by contacting the HWUM Finance Office. Please ensure your fees are settled on time to avoid late payment penalties or restrictions on your academic account.

All fees are payable in advance [1]. Full settlement of your first semester fee is required upon registration or by the intake date [1]. Fees for subsequent semesters must be paid according to the due dates stated in the payment schedule or on your tuition fee invoice [1][4].

Yes, Heriot-Watt University Malaysia allows students to pay their tuition fees in instalments. Instalment plans are typically structured on a per-semester basis, subject to approval by the Finance Office. To apply or learn more about the available payment schedules and terms, please contact the Finance Department or visit the Student Service Centre before the fee payment deadline.

Yes, you may pay your tuition fee by instalment [1]. The university offers a 6-month instalment payment option using a Maybank credit card issued in Malaysia [1]. This plan is interest-free, requires a minimum charge of RM15,000, and includes a RM200 university administration fee [1]. You can apply for the instalment plan through the University Online Payment System via the myHWU Apps or at https://studentpayments.hw.ac.uk [1].

You can pay your tuition fees online via the Heriot-Watt Online Payment Portal or through Flywire, which is recommended for international payments. Local students can also pay using JomPAY or FPX online banking by including their Student ID as the reference. To access the direct payment links and view your outstanding balance, please log in to the Student Portal. If you require further assistance, you can contact the Student Financial Services team at MYFinance@hw.ac.uk.

Online payments via debit/credit card or direct bank transfer can be made through the Heriot-Watt Online Payment System on myHWU Apps or at https://studentpayments.hw.ac.uk [1]. To pay, you can select outstanding invoices or enter an amount for advanced payment before proceeding to pay [2]. When selecting your payment method, you can choose to pay "By Card" or "By Bank Transfer" [4]. Clicking your preferred option will direct you to a secured payment platform where you fill in your details to complete the payment [4].

You can contact the Finance Office at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia by emailing **myfinance@hw.ac.uk** regarding your fee payment receipts. Please include your full name, Student ID number, and proof of payment in the email to help speed up the process.

To request an official payment receipt, you should email the Student Service Centre (SSC) at student-services-malaysia@hw.ac.uk [1]. Additionally, when submitting a payment receipt, you should email it to your Education Consultant and HWUM@hw.ac.uk [4].

During the semester, the Heriot-Watt University Malaysia Library closes at 6:00 PM on Saturdays (operating from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM). Please note that opening hours may vary during semester breaks, exam periods, or public holidays.

For specific inquiries regarding your fee statement, please contact the HWUM Finance Office at hwum-finance@hw.ac.uk.

Your honours degree classification is calculated based on the weighted average of your marks achieved in your upper stages of study (typically Stages 3 and 4). Generally, a First Class requires an average mark of 70% or above, an Upper Second (2:1) is 60–69%, a Lower Second (2:2) is 50–59%, and a Third Class is 40–49%. The exact weighting ratio applied between stages depends on your specific programme structure. Please check your programme handbook or consult your Academic Advisor for the precise calculation formula for your course.

Eligible applicants can also apply for the Deputy Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship, Future Leaders Scholarship, and various financial hardship bursaries. Additionally, family discounts, alumni discounts, and external sponsorships (such as MARA and JPA) are available. For detailed eligibility criteria and application deadlines, please visit the official HWUM website or contact our admissions team.
